title: Invoice Intake Agent
outcome: 50 synthetic invoices checked in 1.4 s: all 8 planted errors stopped, none wrongly approved, 142 of 150 keying minutes removed.
summary: Accounts payable teams key supplier invoices by hand at about three minutes each. I built a Python agent that reads PDF invoices, checks them against vendor and PO master data, and only sends exceptions to a person, then mapped it to AI Builder, Power Automate, Dataverse and Copilot Studio. The benchmark uses the rule-based reader; the Claude extraction path was not part of that run.
cv: Inspired by: P&O integration analytics into governed single-source datasets.

cards.title: Watch the run
cards.caption: 28 seconds from the demo video: the inbox, one click, and the results with reasons.

description.text: Silent, 28 seconds, with on-screen captions. 0:00 The Invoice intake agent app shows an empty run: 0 invoices processed. Caption: "Here is the inbox: fifty synthetic invoices in three different layouts, with a few deliberate errors hidden inside." 0:08 The user clicks Run intake. Caption: "One click." 0:09 The tiles fill in: 50 processed, 84% auto-approved, 8 waiting for review, 2.4 hours saved, with a bar chart of outcomes and of why invoices need a person. Caption: "Fifty invoices are read and checked in under two seconds. By hand, that is about two and a half hours of keying." 0:16 Caption: "Forty two passed every control and were approved automatically." 0:20 The exception queue is shown. Caption: "Eight need a person, and the agent says why: an amount that differs from the purchase order, an unknown vendor, a duplicate, or wrong VAT."

cards.title: AI pair programming
cards.body: Developed with AI pair programming, not GitHub Copilot. The benchmark figures come from a fresh run of the original build. The Power Platform version is a written design and has not been deployed.
